title: Ordinary etale projective bundle and Chern identities over Noetherian bases
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme on which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and roots-of-unity twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. A vector bundle means a finite locally free module [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. For a rank-$r>0$ vector bundle $F$, let $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\operatorname{Sym}F)\to X$ be the projective bundle of line quotients [def-nagata-relative-proj], and put $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, where $c_1$ is the Kummer boundary of the frame torsor [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Then
$$(1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{r-1}\Lambda_X(-a)[-2a]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\Lambda_P.$$
There are unique classes $c_i(F)\in H^{2i}(X,\Lambda(i))$ satisfying $c_0(F)=1$, $c_i(F)=0$ for $i>r$, and
$$\xi^r-p^*c_1(F)\xi^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^rp^*c_r(F)=0.$$
For rank zero set $c_0=1$ and $c_i=0$ for $i>0$. They agree with the Kummer first Chern class for lines, commute with pullback, and satisfy $c_t(F)=c_t(F')c_t(F'')$ for every short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, where $c_t(F)=\sum_i c_i(F)t^i$. Moreover $c_i(F^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(F)$. The projective bundle decomposition and all these classes commute with reduction $\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ for $N\geq n$, using $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$ on roots of unity. The displayed cup products are the derived-tensor products on ordinary etale cohomology. No regularity or field-of-definition hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Propositions 1.4 and 1.7; coefficient compatibility of the Kummer construction and the uniquely determined projective-bundle coefficients.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary Kummer class of a line $L$ from its frame torsor and [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. The frame torsor of a tensor product is the contracted product by [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. Additivity and dual signs may also be read directly from [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] with full support and the unique trivialization on the empty complement: $c_1(LM)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$ and $c_1(L^\vee)=-c_1(L)$. For $g:T\to X$, the pulled-back transition functions of the frame torsor are $g^*g_{ij}$; [lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality] identifies their torsor class with pullback followed by the units map. This units map gives a morphism from the inverse-image Kummer sequence to the Kummer sequence on $T$. Naturality of its boundary [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] proves $g^*c_1(L)=c_1(g^*L)$. Roots, tensor products and evaluations have exactly the pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].

source.place: XVI Definition 1.1 and the additivity/pullback paragraph, pp.225-226; full-support instance of the admitted supported-product interface

proof.text: For a rank-$r>0$ bundle form $p:P\to X$ with its tautological line by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry] and put $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$. For each $0\le a<r$, tensor $a$ copies of $h:\Lambda_P\to\Lambda_P(1)[2]$ and evaluate against $p^{-1}\Lambda_X(-a)[-2a]$. Adjunction gives a component $\Lambda_X(-a)[-2a]\to Rp_*\Lambda_P$; take their finite sum $\Phi_F$. These are the derived-tensor cup powers in the statement [def-kun-derived-tensor, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Under any base change the actual exchange mate [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] sends each pulled component to the corresponding component for $g^*F$: its adjunct is the pulled cup power, since counit cancels unit. Step 1 and tautological base change identify that cup power with $c_1(\mathcal O(1))^a$ on the new bundle. Proper exchange is invertible by [prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Thus $\operatorname{Ex}\,g^{-1}\Phi_F=\Phi_{g^*F}$. This constructs and compares the named morphisms before proving them invertible.

source.place: XVI Theorem 1.2; agent expansion of the global cup-power map and its exchange equation

proof.text: We first establish $\Phi$ over a geometric field of positive characteristic $p\ne\ell$. On $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, apply [thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula] only to the free bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and coefficient level $n$. Its coefficient ring is then $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The ordinary/pro-etale Kummer identification in [lem-pur-kummer-additivity] and finite-root identification in [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] identify its class with the comparison image of step 1, including its positive sign. The direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] identifies the image of $\Phi^{\mathrm{et}}$ with this isomorphism: its displayed counit equality identifies adjuncts; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies their cup powers. The comparison is fully faithful [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], so $\Phi^{\mathrm{et}}$ is invertible. For an arbitrary algebraically closed $K$ of characteristic $p$, take a common algebraically closed extension of $K$ and $k$ over $\mathbf F_p$. Such an extension is obtained by taking a prime quotient of the nonzero tensor product of the two fields and then an algebraic closure of its fraction field. Step 2 and proper geometric exchange [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identify both base changes with the same map. The exact sections/stalk identification of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology] makes pullback between algebraically closed points faithful on cohomology; hence $\Phi$ over $K$ is invertible too.

source.place: Theorem 1.2, geometric-field reduction; replace its external field calculation by the admitted finite-field projective-bundle theorem, with explicit site/normalization comparisons

proof.text: Fix $m\ge0$, put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/\ell]$ and $q:\mathbf P^m_B\to B$, and form $\Phi_B$ as in step 2. It is proper by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. Its standard opens have rings $R[T_j/T_i:j\ne i]$ by [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]; these are affine $m$-spaces, so [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth, lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] make $q$ smooth. The constant abelian sheaf $G=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ is locally constant and every stalk element has order a power of the unit $\ell$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-acyclicity] followed by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-torsion-local-acyclicity] makes $q$ locally acyclic relative to $G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-locally-acyclic-specialization], every specialization $(R^jq_*G)_{\bar s}\to(R^jq_*G)_{\bar t}$ through the strict localization of $B$ is an isomorphism. The theorem applies to the whole torsion sheaf $G$, for every $n$, rather than just prime coefficients.

source.place: Tags 0GJQ proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic, 0GJR lemma-locally-acyclic-locally-constant and 0GJW lemma-sp-isom-proper-torsion-loc-ac; application to polynomial projective space

proof.text: Choose a closed point $\bar s$ of $B$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$. The strict henselization $H$ of $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Thus $H\otimes\mathbf Q\ne0$; a prime quotient followed by a fraction field and algebraic closure gives a characteristic-zero geometric point $\bar t$ of $B_{(\bar s)}$. The specialization square for $\mathcal H^j(\Phi_B)$ commutes: both stalk maps restrict the same pointed-neighbourhood representatives, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-locally-acyclic-specialization]. On the source, specialization is invertible since each $\Lambda(-a)$ is locally constant [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; trivialize it on a pointed etale neighbourhood and the restriction map is identity. On the target it is invertible by step 4. Step 3 and proper stalk exchange [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] give invertibility at $\bar s$, hence at $\bar t$. Every other characteristic-zero geometric field and this field have a common algebraically closed extension over $\mathbf Q$, constructed as in step 3. Step 2 and proper exchange therefore give the same result over every such field. No finite-field scheme structure on a characteristic-zero field has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, specialization map as restriction of pointed-neighbourhood germs; Tag 07QM for faithful flatness; agent application to the global Kummer-power map

proof.text: For the original $p:P(F)\to X$, take any geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$. The pullback of $F$ is a free rank-$r$ vector space; [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry] identifies its projective bundle and line with $(\mathbf P_K^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$. By step 2 and [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], the stalk of $\Phi_F$ is precisely its cup-power decomposition. Steps 3 and 5 prove it invertible in both possible characteristics. Underlying abelian complexes are bounded below, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] therefore makes $\Phi_F$ an isomorphism; [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] detects this in the module category as well. This proves the displayed projective-bundle formula over every Noetherian $X$, and step 2 already proves its pullback equation.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] with the global-sections topos to identify R Gamma_X R p_* with R Gamma_P. Twist the decomposition of step 6 by $\Lambda_X(r)[2r]$ and apply ordinary cohomology. The twists are flat invertible lines [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] identifies this with the map $\bigoplus_{a=0}^{r-1}H^{2(r-a)}(X,\Lambda(r-a))\to H^{2r}(P,\Lambda(r))$, $(b_a)\mapsto\sum_a p^*b_a h^a$. The hypotheses of this projection theorem hold: $p$ is proper, hence finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Expand $h^r$ uniquely in this basis and define $c_i(F)=(-1)^{i+1}b_{r-i}$ for $1\le i\le r$. Set $c_0=1$ and $c_i=0$ for $i>r$, also for rank zero. This gives exactly the monic relation and its uniqueness. For $r=1$, $P(F)=X$ and its tautological line is $F$ by the same geometry node, so the coefficient is its Kummer class. Pull back the relation using steps 1-2; uniqueness over the new base proves naturality of every $c_i$.

source.place: XVI proof of Theorem 1.3, p.227: uniquely defined monic coefficients and the rank-one case

proof.text: We prove the line-root formula for an arbitrary filtration $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F$ by subbundles with line quotients $L_i$. On $P=P(F)$ put $Y_i=P(F/F_i)$, so $Y_0=P$ and $Y_r=\varnothing$. The tautological-quotient classification [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] identifies $Y_i$ with the zero locus in $Y_{i-1}$ of $p^*L_i\to\mathcal O(1)$: a quotient of $F/F_{i-1}$ kills its line subbundle $L_i$ exactly when it factors through $F/F_i$. In an adapted local frame its equations are the first $i$ homogeneous coordinates. Thus these are nested closed subschemes; no assertion based only on set-theoretic images is used. On $Y_{i-1}\setminus Y_i$, that line map is an isomorphism, since locally its coefficient is an invertible coordinate. It trivializes $M_i=(\mathcal O_P(1)\otimes p^*L_i^\vee)|_{Y_{i-1}}$. All these schemes are Noetherian by properness and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Hence the supported Kummer class of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] gives $\beta_i\in H^2_{Y_i}(Y_{i-1},\Lambda(1))$ whose image is $(h-p^*c_1(L_i))|_{Y_{i-1}}$.

source.place: XVI Lemma 1.6 and Section 2.1: agent extension of its hyperplane argument to a filtration using the admitted nested-support products

proof.text: Write $\alpha_i=h-p^*c_1(L_i)$. Start with $e_0=1\in H^0_P(P,\Lambda)$. Inductively define $e_i=\beta_i\cdot e_{i-1}\in H^{2i}_{Y_i}(P,\Lambda(i))$ using the nested action of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], with $Z=Y_i$, $Y=Y_{i-1}$ and ambient scheme $P$. Its projection formula says that after enlarging support from $Y_i$ to $Y_{i-1}$ this is multiplication of $e_{i-1}$ by $\alpha_i$: the image of $\beta_i$ on $Y_{i-1}$ is the restriction of $\alpha_i$. Therefore, after forgetting all support, $e_i$ maps to $\alpha_1\cdots\alpha_i$; this is an induction from $e_0=1$, not a splitting assertion about $F$. Since $Y_r$ is empty, its supported-sections functor is zero by [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]; hence $e_r=0$. We obtain $\prod_i(h-p^*c_1(L_i))=0$. Comparing its coefficients with the unique monic relation in step 7 proves $c_t(F)=\prod_i(1+c_1(L_i)t)$ for every such filtration, including nonsplit ones. All degrees are even, so no additional commutation sign enters.

source.place: XVI Lemma 1.6 and Section 2.1; explicit nested-support induction in place of an extension-splitting torsor

proof.text: Use the recursive flag construction [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle]. Each stage is a projective bundle and its pullback admits the indicated next line quotient. By step 6, the unit $\Lambda_T\to Rq_*\Lambda_{P(G)}$ is inclusion of the $a=0$ summand and has retraction the corresponding projection. Tensoring with $\Lambda_T(b)$ and applying [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] gives a retraction for every twisted unit. Using the same derived-composition statement for global sections, the pullback on $H^j(T,\Lambda(b))$ is injective: a class mapping to zero is recovered as zero by that retraction. Iterating proves injectivity along the whole flag map. All bases remain Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; properness is supplied by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. This derives the necessary cohomological splitting principle from step 6, without using a finite-field-only flag theorem.

source.place: XVI Proposition 1.4, pp.226-227: flag tower and split injection from the projective-bundle formula

proof.text: For $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, pull back first to the complete flag bundle of $F'$, then to that of the pulled-back $F''$. Step 10 makes this composite injective on every relevant cohomology group. On this base, combine the flag of $F'$ with the inverse images in $F$ of the flag of $F''$. These inverse images are subbundles: locally the original exact sequence splits because its quotient is finite free, and local adapted bases exhibit each term and its quotient as free. The resulting line quotients of $F$ are exactly the two lists of flag quotients. Step 9 therefore identifies $c_t(F)$ with the product of those two root polynomials, which are $c_t(F')$ and $c_t(F'')$ by the same step. Step 7 gives pullback naturality, and injectivity descends this equality to $X$. For duality, pull $F$ to its complete flag bundle. Dualizing the flag in reverse order gives a subbundle filtration of $F^\vee$ with line quotients $L_i^\vee$. Step 1 negates each line class. Step 9 then gives $c_t(F^\vee)=c_{-t}(F)$ there, and step 10 descends it. The coefficient of $t^i$ is the required $(-1)^ic_i(F)$. Empty root lists handle rank-zero bundles. If ranks vary, take the finitely many open-and-closed rank strata; cohomology of their disjoint union is the product, so these equalities give the global equality.

source.place: XVI Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 1.7, pp.227-228; elementary assembly from steps 7-10

proof.text: For $N\ge n$, compare the two Kummer sequences at exponents $\ell^N$ and $\ell^n$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. The left vertical map is $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{N-n}}$, the middle vertical map on $\mathbf G_m$ is the same power, and the right vertical map is identity. The right square commutes since $(z^{\ell^{N-n}})^{\ell^n}=z^{\ell^N}$. Naturality of the connecting maps [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] carries the boundary of the unchanged frame-torsor class to its level-$n$ boundary. The left map is exactly the root-twist reduction of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Tensor powers and evaluations respect that reduction, and the supported-product calculus says the cup products commute with coefficient reduction [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. Thus the same is true for all components of $\Phi_F$ and for the monic relation. Reducing its coefficients gives a monic relation at level $n$; step 7's uniqueness proves reduction of every $c_i(F)$. This proves compatibility without assuming flatness of $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^N$. If the decomposition is read via derived scalar extension, its target comparison is the canonical proper projection/scalar mate of [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection, lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]; these identify scalar extension of the components with the same level-$n$ cup powers. The scalar-mate boundedness assumptions hold since the already proved decomposition is a finite sum of shifted flat Tate lines; its scalar extension is again such a sum.
